title: Single generic query_soccer SQL tool instead of discrete per-capability MCP tools
evidence: server.c:114-125 registers one tool query_soccer taking a raw SQL string; capabilities R3-R11 are satisfied by client-authored SELECTs over the schema documented in data.c:6-14, not by named per-query handlers
suggestion: Legitimate pattern and all capabilities are reachable+tested; if the spec intends discoverable per-query tools, expose thin named wrappers in addition to the SQL endpoint

title: FIFA players table is a single undated snapshot, so player-to-standings joins are point-in-time
evidence: data.c:152 imports fifa_data as players with no season column; test_soccer.py:90 joins players to standings season=2019 by team_key(Club) with no temporal alignment
suggestion: Acceptable given the dataset; document that player ratings/clubs are a single snapshot not aligned to match seasons

title: Cross-source match dedup relies on a +/-1 day date-window heuristic
evidence: data.c:160-173 builds matches by NOT EXISTS against reports within date(r.date,'-1 day')..('+1 day') and back-fills postponed games only when exactly one candidate exists
suggestion: Works for the test assertions (e.g. 18 Copa do Brasil finals); note the fuzzy join could mis-pair fixtures replayed within a day across datasets
